text:
### Observed differences

- The choice of branch after A20 flipped. In the earlier window, about 82 in 100 of A20's outgoing continuations went to A24 (~29%), A25 (~24%) or A26 (~29%), and only about 18 in 100 to A21, A22 or A23; in the later window, about 79 in 100 go to A21 (~29%), A22 (~22%) or A23 (~29%), while A24–A26 take about 21 in 100. [DIR020]
- Participation mirrors this swap: A24, A25 and A26 appeared in about 82 in 100 traces earlier but only about 21 in 100 later, while A21, A22 and A23 rose from about 19 in 100 to about 79 in 100 traces. [OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, OCC025]
- The two three-activity blocks swapped their "executed together" behaviour: earlier, A24/A25/A26 co-occurred in about 82 in 100 traces and A21/A22/A23 in only about 18 in 100; later, A21/A22/A23 co-occur in about 79 in 100 traces, appearing in both orders in similar shares (no fixed internal order), while A24/A25/A26 co-occurrence dropped to about 21 in 100. [REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL020, REL021, REL028, REL041, REL042, REL046]
- Co-occurrence with A30, which appears in every trace in both windows, flipped the same way: A21/A22/A23 now co-occur with A30 in about 79 in 100 traces (earlier about 19 in 100), A24/A25/A26 in about 21 in 100 (earlier about 82 in 100). [REL025, REL032, REL038, REL043, REL047, REL050]
- Event positions of the six activities barely moved (mean positions around 0.66–0.68 of the trace in both windows); only the share of traces containing them changed. [POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- A10 became rarer and its placement changed: it appeared in about 17 in 100 traces earlier but about 7 in 100 later; its median event position moved from about 0.86 to 0.36 with much higher spread; and its outgoing transitions changed from almost always A33 (~97%) to a spread over A14/A15/A16/A20/A27/A34/A35. These rest on only 33 versus 14 traces. [OCC010, POS001, DIR010, REL001]
- Several rare activities became somewhat more frequent — A02 (about 2→9 in 100 traces), A04 (about 1.5→8.5), A06 (about 2→6) and A08 (about 1→6.5) — with completely changed successor profiles, but the underlying counts are small (2–4 earlier, 12–18 later). [OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC008, DIR002, DIR004, DIR006, DIR008]
- Repetition increased modestly: A15 and A16 averaged about 1.69 occurrences per trace earlier versus about 1.88 later while still appearing in every trace, and A32/A33 participation rose from about 60 to about 70 in 100 traces. [OCC015, OCC016, OCC030, OCC031]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the routing after A20 changed: in the earlier window, about 80 in 100 traces continued from A20 into the block A24–A25–A26, which typically executed together within one trace, whereas in the later window about 79 in 100 traces continue from A20 into the block A21–A22–A23, which now typically executes together without a fixed internal order, while A24–A26 persist as a rarer alternative (about 21 in 100 traces). All six activities are observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows (about 19–82 in 100) and their event positions are essentially unchanged, so this is a change in how often existing alternative paths are taken, not a relocation, addition or removal of activities. [DIR020, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, OCC025, REL011, REL014, REL020, REL028, REL041, POS003, POS006]

The change is direct and consistent across indicator families: A20's outgoing transition shares flip (about 82% → 21% to A24/A25/A26 and about 18% → 79% to A21/A22/A23, with 200 traces per window), the participation of all six activities moves by roughly 60 percentage points, A20 precedes A21/A22/A23 in about 77–79 in 100 traces later (versus about 18–19 earlier) and precedes A24/A25/A26 in about 21 versus 81, and within-block co-occurrence and co-occurrence with A30 flip in the same direction. [DIR020, OCC020, OCC023, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL025, REL032, REL038, REL043, REL047, REL050]

Limitations: the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows mix different process variants or subpopulations rather than reflecting a single rerouting, and because A21/A22/A23 appear in both orders in similar proportions, no fixed sequence within the new block can be inferred. [REL020, REL021, REL028]

Other differences: A10 became rarer (about 17 → 7 in 100 traces), appears earlier in the trace (median event position about 0.86 → 0.36) and its successors changed from almost always A33 to a spread of activities; this rests on 33 versus 14 traces and is not part of the main hypothesis. [OCC010, POS001, DIR010] The rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A08 became somewhat more frequent (about 1–2 → 6–9 in 100 traces) with markedly changed successor profiles, but the underlying counts are small (2–4 versus 12–18 traces). [OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC008, DIR002, DIR004, DIR006, DIR008] Repetition increased somewhat, with A15 and A16 averaging about 1.69 → 1.88 occurrences per trace while appearing in every trace, and A32/A33 participation rising to about 70 in 100 traces. [OCC015, OCC016, OCC030, OCC031]
